newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fell in week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fell in week.

text.p: U.S. mortgage rates fell this week on continuing signs of economic growth with no inflationary pressures, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year mortgage rates averaged 7.47 percent in the week ended July 11, down from 7.62 percent last week. Fifteen-year mortgage rates fell to 7.01 percent from 7.15 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates also declined, to 5.53 percent from 5.67 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.42 percent, the 15-year 7.93 percent and the adjustable loan 6.01 percent.
"As we predicted, mortgage interest rates lowered considerably this week," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said in a statement.
"Homeownership is made even more affordable for a greater amount of families whenever interest rates fall, and we expect these low rates will translate into continuing robust housing sales."

Fees and points charged by lenders for 30-year loans remained unchanged at an average 1.8 percent. Fifteen-year loans edged up to 1.8 percent from 1.7 percent last week. Adjustable rates were unchanged at 1.4 percent.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
